clue.text: Still, it's pictures were enchanting

parts.note: reads as a remark about films, but describes an old projector whose still pictures came from an 'enchanting' (spellbinding) device

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb 'yet'; it is the adjective, as in still (not moving) pictures, which the Victorian projector showed. 'Enchanting' points at the first word of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This early slide projector threw still images painted on glass onto a screen, a source of wonder to its audiences.

clue.text: Chump introducing Stanley to this horse

indicators.note: the chump word brings the name into its middle, holding it inside

parts.note: a mug is a chump, a fool
Stan is short for Stanley

explanation.surface: A fool brings Stanley over to meet a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' looks like a social introduction of Stanley to the horse; it means the chump word takes the name into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Look flashy-note dressing

parts.note: G is a musical note
lint is cloth used to dress wounds

explanation.surface: A note on how to dress to look flashy.
explanation.definitionFit: To glint is to flash or sparkle briefly with light.

clue.text: A discount arranged for the warden

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warden sets up a reduced price.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper or guardian of a building or collection is in charge of it.

clue.text: Prophet admits his generous proportions

parts.note: the prophet admits 'I am', so the word am comes from his admission
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, generous proportions

explanation.surface: A biblical figure confesses he is rather large.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophet admits 'I AM OS': AM, then OS, the label for outsize clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible in his name.

clue.text: Bearer of current tidings?

parts.note: 'current' reads as up-to-date but also means electric current, which carried a wired message

explanation.definitionFit: A message sent by electric telegraph wire and delivered on paper.

clue.text: A metal worker?

parts.note: reads as a smith or welder but means a worker made of metal, a machine

explanation.definitionFit: A machine built to do work in place of a person.

clue.text: Without a starting signal, jolly stupid

parts.note: 'go!' is the signal to start
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
less means without

explanation.surface: Lacking any signal to begin, someone looks very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like 'very' qualifying 'stupid'; it is a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word for lacking sense or understanding.

clue.text: Some poetry about right way to reduce ?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the verb, a way of losing weight

indicators.note: about means going round, so the poetry word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a stave is a stanza, some poetry

explanation.surface: A poem about the right way to slim.
explanation.walkthrough: A stave is a verse or stanza; 'about' wraps it round the R. The definition is a phrase standing for the verb, a means of slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food is a drastic method of losing weight.

clue.text: William Tell part, say, one can get one's teeth into

definitions.text: one can get one's teeth into

indicators.note: 'say' tells us to take the phrase as spoken and write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss folk hero, so playing him is a Swiss role

explanation.surface: An actor relishes playing William Tell, a part to really get stuck into.
explanation.walkthrough: A Swiss role sounds like the rolled sponge cake. 'Something to get one's teeth into' usually means a demanding task; here it is literal, a cake you bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled sponge cake filled with jam or cream is something you literally bite into.

clue.text: Push makes Kipling's African marchers turn tail

indicators.note: the tail, the last two letters, of the marchers' word is turned round

parts.note: Kipling's poem 'Boots' is about infantry marching in South Africa, with the refrain 'boots, boots, boots'

explanation.surface: Kipling's soldiers retreat while being pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn tail' swaps the last two letters of BOOTS, giving BOOST. Kipling's poem 'Boots' (from the Boer War) repeats the word to suggest marching feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a boost is to give them a push upwards or forwards.

clue.text: What's done in court

parts.note: reads as courtroom conduct but means both a deed done and a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, and a lawsuit brought before a judge is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Sands running out for a wall-squatter?

definitions.text: Sands running out for a wall-squatter?

parts.words: Sands running out for a wall-squatter?
parts.note: the sands of a small hourglass run out to time the boiling of an egg, and an egg (Humpty Dumpty) famously sat on a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped 'for a'; the page has it. Humpty Dumpty, the nursery-rhyme egg, 'sat on a wall', so the wall-squatter is an egg, and the sand device times it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass that runs for about three minutes is used to time boiling an egg.

clue.text: Talk of male chauvinist brutes, so unsettling!

indicators.note: something unsettling is disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: 'male chauvinist pigs' is the stock insult, so the brutes are pigs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A protest about sexist men's chatter that disturbs everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk about other people's affairs is tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Final clue follower

parts.note: reads as a detective's last lead, but means what follows the last clue in a puzzle: the printed answers

explanation.definitionFit: The answers printed after a puzzle's last clue resolve it.

clue.text: Money, pure and simple, to keep you warm

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the fine wool does, standing for the noun

parts.note: cash is money
mere means nothing more than, as in 'a mere child'

explanation.surface: Advice that money, plainly and simply, is what keeps you comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine soft goat wool is prized for warm jumpers and scarves.

clue.text: Has let many inside for the feast

indicators.note: inside means the following pieces go within the word has

parts.note: taken as written
allow means let
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

explanation.surface: A host admits a crowd to the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: HALLOWMAS is the old name for All Saints' Day; 'inside' puts the verb for let and the Roman numeral for a thousand within the clue's 'Has'.
explanation.definitionFit: All Saints' Day on 1 November is an old church feast day.

clue.text: Remove possible gold inside perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: Remove possible gold inside perhaps (8): the parse is GOLD anagrammed ('possible') inside SIDE anagrammed ('perhaps'), D-IS-LODG-E, so the one word 'inside' is both the container indicator and the fodder SIDE

clue.text: Opposed to entering last cataclysm, it was overwhelmed

indicators.note: one piece is going into another, so it sits inside the rearranged letters
a cataclysm is an upheaval, so the letters of the word next to it are thrown about

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: In a final disaster, something hostile breaks in and swamps everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cataclysm' scrambles the word last to ATLS, and 'entering' sets the word for opposed to inside it, after its third letter. The definition is the legendary sunken island.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary island was said to have been swallowed by the sea in a single day.

clue.text: A Catholic peer's son as an Athenian magistrate

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
a peer's son is styled the Hon, Honourable

explanation.surface: A Catholic nobleman's son serving as a magistrate in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the nine chief officials who governed ancient Athens.

clue.text: Like certain shops near Land's End

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: the end of the word Land's is its final letter, taken alone

explanation.surface: Describing shops close to Land's End, the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far south-western tip of England, in Cornwall; here only its last letter is wanted. 'Land's' counts as LAND, so the end is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops are shut on early-closing day or in a closed-shop sense where only union members work.

clue.text: "That deep-brow'd Homer ruled as his ——" (Keats)

definitions.text: That deep-brow'd Homer ruled as his ——" (Keats

parts.words: That deep-brow'd Homer ruled as his ——" (Keats
parts.note: a line from Keats's sonnet On First Looking into Chapman's Homer, whose missing last word is the poet's realm

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank from Keats's sonnet: 'One wide expanse ... That deep-brow'd Homer ruled as his ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate or domain held and ruled by its lord.

clue.text: Weapon gives a light blow causing schism in sect

indicators.note: a schism splits a body, so the sect's word is split open to take the blow inside

parts.note: a cult is a sect
a tap is a light blow

explanation.surface: A weapon whose small strike splits a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing schism in' splits the sect word open, with a light blow and A put into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with elastic, or the siege engine, hurls stones.

clue.text: Warm wear for flood precaution In Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in means the flood precaution sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Noah's ark was the precaution against the Flood

explanation.surface: Advice on clothing to wear against floods in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts Noah's vessel inside the state abbreviation; 'flood precaution' reads as sandbags but means the vessel built against the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded windproof jacket worn in cold weather.

clue.text: Gun dogs ?

explanation.definitionFit: A quick-firing anti-aircraft gun was named for its sound, and two Pomeranian dogs are each a 'Pom'.

clue.text: Shoot to get a lemur

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving African primate of the loris family, loosely called a lemur.

clue.text: The French in the Diplomatic Corps are so dressed

indicators.note: in means the French article sits inside the diplomats' abbreviation

parts.note: CD is Corps Diplomatique, the Diplomatic Corps
la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: French diplomats who are well turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the French for 'the' inside the diplomats' abbreviation, CD for Corps Diplomatique.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothed, as in 'clad in silk'.

clue.text: If it's bad, Stinker's in it

definitions.text: If it's bad, Stinker's in it

parts.words: If it's bad, Stinker's in it
parts.note: a smell that is bad is a stink, so the stinker is found in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinker' looks like a person in trouble ('in it' as in 'in for it'); it is a bad smell itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell or scent, which when unpleasant is a stink.

clue.text: The range is the same, see, with the little ones

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
lo is an old word for 'see!'
mites are little ones, tiny children

explanation.surface: A family trip to the mountains, repeated, with the children along.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, used in lists to mean 'the same again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain range of the north-eastern Italian Alps.

clue.text: Revolutionary pattern-changing cylinder -

parts.note: 'revolutionary' suggests politics but means turned round and round, a tube whose pattern alters as it rotates

explanation.definitionFit: A tube of mirrors and coloured glass that shows shifting symmetrical patterns when turned.
